body:
Psalm 45 speaks of love and belonging. Corinthians reminds us that “the world in its present form is passing away.” Then Jesus says something startling in Luke: blessed are the poor, the hungry, those who weep—and woe to those who are already satisfied.

What is God trying to tell us?

Perhaps he is asking: Where have you placed your heart?

We spend so much of life believing that when something finally changes, we will be whole. When I find the right person. When my marriage gets better. When I have enough money. When my health improves. When my career works out. Then I will have peace.

But Paul says: meet God where you are. Married or single, comfortable or struggling, fulfilled or disappointed—this present life is passing away. None of these things were meant to become our final security.

And perhaps that is why Jesus calls the hungry blessed. Hunger makes us reach for something beyond ourselves. The danger of being completely satisfied is believing we no longer need anything—or anyone.

Our circumstances will change. People will come and go. Success can disappear. Bodies grow older. Plans unravel. But none of these things determine where our story ends.

The question is whether, through all of it, we continue choosing God.

Maybe the blessing is not always getting what we thought would make us whole. Maybe sometimes the blessing is discovering that what we were reaching for could never completely satisfy us anyway.

God is not merely part of the journey. He is the destination.
prayer: Lord, when I become too attached to the things of this world, remind me that they are passing. When I am hungry, grieving, uncertain, or disappointed, help me recognize that you are still near. Teach me to seek you above everything else and to trust that whatever changes around me, my heart can remain anchored in you. Amen.
title: What is God trying to tell us!
